cultural_note: Same root as "se plaindre" (to complain), but a different construction with a different meaning — plain "plaindre" is about pitying someone else, while the reflexive form is about voicing one's own grievance.

translation_en: rye (the grain crop, used especially for dark/rye bread)
definition_in_language: Céréale utilisée notamment pour fabriquer du pain, à la mie plus sombre que le blé.
source_sentence: Ensuite le Bon visita la campagne, plaignit les huguenots de la maigreur de leurs récoltes et se réjouit de ce qu'à tout le moins l'année avait été bonne pour le seigle.

translation_en: hail (the weather phenomenon — ice pellets falling during a storm)
definition_in_language: Précipitation de grains de glace tombant du ciel lors d'un orage.
cultural_note: Same spelling also exists as an unrelated adjective meaning "thin, spindly, gaunt" (of a body, voice, or limb) — similar in meaning to "fluet," added earlier — two unrelated words sharing one spelling.

translation_en: to dig (with a pickaxe); figuratively (informal), to grind/study hard
definition_in_language: Creuser la terre avec une pioche ; au sens figuré et familier, travailler dur, notamment étudier avec application.
cultural_note: From "pioche," added earlier. The figurative sense is common student slang — "piocher ses cours" = to cram/study hard.

translation_en: oats (the grain crop)
definition_in_language: Céréale utilisée notamment pour l'alimentation animale et humaine (flocons d'avoine, porridge).

translation_en: chicory (a plant — its bitter leaves are eaten as a salad green, and its roasted root is used as a coffee substitute/additive)
definition_in_language: Plante dont on consomme les feuilles en salade (souvent amères), ou dont la racine, torréfiée, sert de substitut ou d'ajout au café.
cultural_note: The roasted root became popular as a coffee substitute/stretcher when real coffee was scarce or expensive, and remains a signature ingredient in New Orleans-style coffee today.

translation_en: a core (of a fruit) or a cob (of corn) — the leftover central part after the edible portion is eaten
definition_in_language: Partie centrale et dure d'un fruit ou d'un épi, qui reste une fois la partie comestible consommée — par exemple, le cœur d'une pomme ou l'épi de maïs une fois les grains enlevés.
source_sentence: Des trognons de maïs, des peaux de pois chiches, ce que tu voudras.
cultural_note: "Trognon de maïs" specifically means the corn cob, not the husk — an easy word to guess wrong given the shape of English "husk."

translation_en: to make up for it, to compensate, to recoup (a loss) — literally "to catch oneself" (from falling)
definition_in_language: Compenser une perte ou un échec, souvent par un moyen détourné ; littéralement, se retenir pour ne pas tomber.
source_sentence: Pour se rattraper, il cacha le reste d'avoine, afin de la vendre pour son compte et déclara que le mulet l'avait déjà finie.
cultural_note: "Vendre pour son compte" here reuses the exact pattern from "vivre pour son compte," added earlier — "for one's own account/benefit."

translation_en: by night, at nighttime (a fairly formal/literary adverb)
definition_in_language: De nuit, pendant la nuit — terme assez soutenu, littéraire.
cultural_note: Less common in everyday speech than simpler alternatives like "la nuit" or "de nuit."

translation_en: (severe) abuse, cruel mistreatment (a formal/legal term for deliberate physical cruelty, toward a person or an animal — almost always plural)
definition_in_language: Mauvais traitements graves et volontaires infligés à une personne ou à un animal, souvent d'ordre physique.
cultural_note: Easy to visually confuse with the completely unrelated everyday word "services" — just one letter apart, very different meaning.

translation_en: a pipe, a tube (water pipe, hose, drainpipe); informally, a tip or inside scoop
definition_in_language: Conduit cylindrique, souvent en métal ou en plastique, servant à faire circuler un liquide ou un gaz.
cultural_note: Very common informal figurative use: "avoir un bon tuyau" = to have a good tip/inside lead (like insider info on something useful).

translation_en: to blur, to muddle, to scramble/mix up (vision, eggs, a signal, thoughts); reflexively, "se brouiller," to fall out with someone
definition_in_language: Rendre trouble, confus ou indistinct ; au sens réfléchi, "se brouiller avec quelqu'un" signifie se fâcher, rompre une relation.
cultural_note: "Œufs brouillés" = scrambled eggs, a common everyday use of the literal sense.

translation_en: flour
definition_in_language: Poudre obtenue en broyant des céréales, comme le blé, utilisée notamment pour faire du pain.

translation_en: a mill (windmill, watermill, or a small grinder like a coffee mill)
definition_in_language: Machine ou bâtiment servant à broyer des grains (comme le blé) pour en faire de la farine, actionné par le vent, l'eau, ou manuellement.
cultural_note: Pairs naturally with "farine," added just before this — the mill is where grain becomes flour.

translation_en: a scribble, a scrawl (messy, hastily-written marks, hard to read)
definition_in_language: Écriture ou dessin fait rapidement et de façon peu soignée, souvent difficile à lire.
cultural_note: From "griffonner," to scribble/scrawl.

translation_en: to smear, to daub, to scrawl (paint, ink, dirt); careless writing/drawing
definition_in_language: Salir ou couvrir grossièrement de peinture, d'encre ou d'une autre substance ; par extension, écrire ou dessiner de façon négligée.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "griffonnage," added just before — same messy-marks territory. Also used figuratively: "avoir l'estomac barbouillé" = to feel queasy/nauseous.

translation_en: a scaffold — specifically an execution platform (guillotine, gallows)
definition_in_language: Plateforme surélevée, destinée aux exécutions capitales (par guillotine, par exemple) — à ne pas confondre avec "échafaudage," structure de construction.
cultural_note: Genuinely distinct from "échafaudage" (construction scaffolding), which appeared earlier in this book's torture-machinery scene ("ces échafaudages de poutres") — similar root, very different meaning.

translation_en: a gibbet — gallows for hanging, or the post where a hanged body was displayed afterward as a warning
definition_in_language: Structure de bois utilisée pour la pendaison des condamnés, ou poteau où l'on exposait le corps d'un pendu.
cultural_note: Near-synonym of "potence," added earlier from this same book.

translation_en: a partition wall (an interior dividing wall, typically lighter than a load-bearing exterior wall)
definition_in_language: Mur intérieur, souvent léger, qui sépare deux pièces ou espaces à l'intérieur d'un bâtiment.

translation_en: a slipknot, a noose (literally "a sliding knot")
definition_in_language: Nœud qui se resserre lorsqu'on tire sur la corde — utilisé notamment pour la pendaison, ou pour tout usage nécessitant un lien ajustable.
cultural_note: The modern, everyday way to say what the archaic word "hart" meant historically — near-synonyms, centuries apart in register.

translation_en: to get the wrong (one) — to be mistaken about which item/choice, not just "to be wrong" in general
definition_in_language: Faire une erreur en choisissant ou en identifiant la mauvaise chose parmi plusieurs — par exemple "se tromper de route" (prendre la mauvaise route) ou "se tromper de jour" (se tromper sur la date).
source_sentence: J'aurais envie qu'on se trompât de moitié.
cultural_note: A very common, everyday construction despite showing up here in an archaic literary tense ("se trompât," imperfect subjunctive) — "se tromper de route," "se tromper de jour," etc. are ordinary modern usage.

translation_en: discord, strife, dissension — almost always in "semer la zizanie" (to sow discord)
definition_in_language: Discorde, mésentente, trouble suscité entre des personnes — surtout dans l'expression "semer la zizanie."
cultural_note: Traces back to the Biblical parable of the wheat and the tares (weeds sown among good crops to choke them out) — "zizanie" was originally the word for that weed itself, and its meaning shifted from "a literal weed causing crop trouble" to "discord" in general.

translation_en: to put to death, to execute
definition_in_language: Exécuter, tuer quelqu'un, généralement dans un cadre officiel ou judiciaire.

translation_en: a conspiracy, a plot (a group secretly banding together, often against a ruler or authority)
definition_in_language: Complot ourdi secrètement par plusieurs personnes, souvent contre une autorité ou un pouvoir établi.
cultural_note: There's also an older, more literal sense — a conjuration/incantation, a magical invocation — but the conspiracy sense is far more common, especially in historical/political contexts like this book.

translation_en: to be plotted, to be hatched, to be brewing (of a scheme or conspiracy)
definition_in_language: Être préparé secrètement, en parlant d'un complot ou d'une machination ; littéralement, "tramer" signifie tisser.
cultural_note: Pairs naturally with "conjuration," added just before — "quelque chose se trame" = "something is afoot/being plotted."

translation_en: heaven be praised, thank heavens (an exclamation of relief/gratitude)
definition_in_language: Expression de soulagement ou de gratitude, signifiant "grâces soient rendues au ciel" — d'origine religieuse, mais souvent employée de façon plus générale.
cultural_note: Religious in origin but often used more loosely, the way English "thank God" gets used even by non-religious speakers.

translation_en: to scold, to reprimand; or, to rumble/growl (thunder, an engine, an angry crowd)
definition_in_language: Réprimander quelqu'un ; ou, au sens propre, produire un bruit sourd et menaçant (tonnerre, moteur) — par extension, se dit d'une foule en colère qui manifeste un mécontentement grondant.
cultural_note: The crowd-rumbling sense ("la foule gronde") fits well with this book's undercurrents of political unrest and conspiracy.

word: en faire voir de toutes les couleurs
translation_en: to give someone a hard time, to put someone through the wringer, to make life difficult for someone
definition_in_language: Faire subir à quelqu'un des difficultés, des tourments ou des tracas répétés — expression imagée pour "faire souffrir, tourmenter."
cultural_note: Literally "to make someone see all the colors" — a vivid image for relentless trouble-causing or harassment.

translation_en: to thrash, to beat up (severely) — a fairly strong, somewhat old-fashioned word
definition_in_language: Battre violemment quelqu'un, lui infliger une correction physique sévère.

translation_en: forked, cloven (split into two prongs — a stick, hooves, or split hair ends)
definition_in_language: Divisé en deux pointes ou branches — se dit d'un sabot, d'une branche, ou même des pointes de cheveux abîmés.
source_sentence: Toi tu te promènes en t'appuyant sur un bâton fourchu.
cultural_note: From "fourche," added earlier (a pitchfork). Also used for a cloven hoof ("sabot fourchu") and split hair ends ("cheveux fourchus").

translation_en: a stick, staff, cane
definition_in_language: Morceau de bois long et rigide, utilisé comme appui pour marcher, comme arme, ou comme outil.
source_sentence: Toi tu te promènes en t'appuyant sur un bâton fourchu.

translation_en: scatterbrained, harebrained, reckless (thoughtless, impulsive, lacking common sense)
definition_in_language: Étourdi, imprudent, qui agit sans réfléchir — littéralement, "qui n'a pas de cervelle."
cultural_note: Literally "de-brained," from "cervelle" (brain) — a vivid, mildly mocking insult.

translation_en: to get someone drunk, to intoxicate; informally, to annoy relentlessly, to wear someone out talking
definition_in_language: Enivrer quelqu'un, le faire boire jusqu'à l'ivresse ; au sens figuré et familier, importuner, agacer quelqu'un de façon insistante.
cultural_note: "Tu me soûles" = "you're driving me crazy/getting on my nerves" — a very common informal use of the figurative sense.

translation_en: to give of oneself tirelessly, to lavish oneself/one's efforts (on someone) — going to great, unrelenting lengths to help
definition_in_language: Se dépenser sans compter pour quelqu'un, faire des efforts constants en sa faveur — de "prodigue," généreux à l'excès.
source_sentence: Il arpentait le village en s'informant minutieusement des besoins de chacun et en ne leur laissant pas de trêve tant qu'il ne s'était pas prodigué pour eux de toutes les façons.
cultural_note: This sentence also uses "trêve" (already in Lexi as "truce") in its broader figurative sense — "respite, letup" — "ne pas laisser de trêve à quelqu'un" = to give someone no rest, not just a literal military truce.

translation_en: to commute, to shuttle back and forth (regularly between two places)
definition_in_language: Faire des allers-retours réguliers entre deux endroits.
cultural_note: From "navette," a shuttle — also the word for a weaving shuttle historically, and for "space shuttle" ("navette spatiale").

translation_en: a hovel, a run-down shack (a dilapidated, crumbling dwelling)
definition_in_language: Habitation en très mauvais état, délabrée.
cultural_note: Near-synonym of "bicoque," added earlier from this same book.

word: fourrer le nez dans les affaires de
translation_en: to stick/poke one's nose into someone's business (meddling, prying)
definition_in_language: Se mêler des affaires d'autrui, être indiscret ou curieux de manière importune.
cultural_note: The French equivalent of the exact same English idiom, image for image.

translation_en: to be scandalized, to be shocked/outraged (by something morally offensive)
definition_in_language: Être choqué, indigné par quelque chose jugé moralement inacceptable.

translation_en: to preach — literally (a religious sermon), or figuratively, to advocate insistently for something
definition_in_language: Prononcer un sermon religieux ; au sens figuré, défendre une idée avec insistance, parfois de façon moralisatrice.

translation_en: to do as one pleases, to act entirely on one's own whim (often with a note of entitlement or high-handedness)
definition_in_language: Agir uniquement selon sa propre volonté, sans se soucier des autres — souvent avec une connotation d'autorité ou de caprice.
cultural_note: "Le bon plaisir" has a historical royal-decree association: "car tel est notre bon plaisir" was the old formal closing phrase of a king's edict, roughly "because that is our royal will" — the phrase still carries a whiff of absolute, unquestionable authority even in everyday modern use.

translation_en: meanness, cruelty, wickedness
definition_in_language: Caractère ou action de quelqu'un qui est méchant, cruel ou malveillant.
cultural_note: Built from the common adjective "méchant" (mean, wicked).

translation_en: a backlash, a boomerang effect, a rebound consequence (close to English "blowback")
definition_in_language: Conséquence négative qui revient frapper celui qui en est à l'origine — l'idée d'un effet boomerang.

translation_en: lascivious, lustful (behavior, glances, or dancing that's sexually suggestive/provocative)
definition_in_language: Qui manifeste un désir sexuel de façon provocante ou immodeste.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "licencieux" and "dévergondé," added earlier from this book.

translation_en: a feast, a big indulgent meal (almost always in "faire ripaille," to feast/gorge oneself)
definition_in_language: Repas copieux et festif, souvent pris avec excès et bonne humeur — surtout dans l'expression "faire ripaille."

translation_en: around, all around (a place) — often following a distance ("ten kilometers around"), or meaning "to everyone present"
definition_in_language: Dans toutes les directions autour d'un lieu ; ou, à tout le monde présent, en faisant le tour.
cultural_note: "Dix kilomètres à la ronde" = "for ten kilometers around"; "il salua tout le monde à la ronde" = "he greeted everyone all around him."

translation_en: a moonlit night
definition_in_language: Nuit éclairée par la lumière de la lune.

translation_en: to become entangled, tangled up, intertwined (literally — branches, hair — or figuratively, a plot or situation growing confused)
definition_in_language: Se mêler de façon confuse, s'emmêler — au sens propre (branches, cheveux) ou au sens figuré (une situation, une intrigue).

translation_en: to hatch (an egg), or to bloom/blossom (a flower opening)
definition_in_language: Sortir de l'œuf, en parlant d'un oisillon ; ou s'ouvrir, en parlant d'une fleur.

translation_en: a lily (the flower)
definition_in_language: Fleur à grands pétales blancs, souvent associée au symbole héraldique de la royauté française (la fleur de lys).
cultural_note: Also spelled "lys" — famously the flower behind the "fleur de lys," the heraldic emblem of the French monarchy.

translation_en: to comply with it, to go along with it, to conform to it ("y" standing in for a rule/expectation already mentioned)
definition_in_language: Se soumettre à quelque chose, agir en accord avec une règle ou une attente déjà évoquée.
cultural_note: "Y" here stands in for "à cela/à ça" — the thing being complied with, already established by context.

translation_en: to catch/trip one's foot on something, to stumble over an obstacle
definition_in_language: Accrocher son pied contre quelque chose et trébucher.
source_sentence: La mère de Pamela allant puiser de l'eau se prit le pied dans un piège et tomba dans le puits.
cultural_note: Don't confuse with "prendre son pied" (no "le," with the possessive "son" instead) — a completely different, informal/slang phrase meaning to have a blast, to get one's kicks (often specifically sexual). Similar-looking, very different meaning.

translation_en: to tame (an animal); figuratively, to win someone over, to gradually make someone comfortable/familiar with you
definition_in_language: Rendre un animal moins craintif, l'habituer à la présence humaine ; au sens figuré, gagner la confiance de quelqu'un peu à peu.
cultural_note: The central verb of the fox scene in Le Petit Prince — "apprivoiser" there means building a bond of trust over time, not domesticating by force.

translation_en: to whistle (with the mouth, or an object — a kettle, wind, a bullet); also, to boo/jeer
definition_in_language: Produire un son aigu en soufflant, avec la bouche ou un objet (sifflet, vent, bouilloire) ; peut aussi signifier huer, exprimer sa désapprobation en sifflant.
cultural_note: "Se faire siffler" = to be booed — in France, whistling at a performance or sports match signals disapproval, the opposite of its meaning in some other cultures. Ties back to "sifflet" (a whistle), added earlier.

translation_en: upside down, topsy-turvy, in complete disarray/chaos
definition_in_language: Dans un désordre complet, bouleversé — se dit d'un lieu en pagaille, ou au figuré de l'état d'esprit de quelqu'un.
cultural_note: A fixed, historically garbled phrase — its literal word-for-word logic doesn't fully parse today, but the meaning (total disorder/chaos) is unambiguous in modern use.

translation_en: to polish, to burnish (weapons, armor); figuratively, "fourbir ses armes" = to prepare for a confrontation
definition_in_language: Nettoyer et polir une arme ou une armure ; au sens figuré, "fourbir ses armes" signifie se préparer à un affrontement.

translation_en: to deck out with flags/bunting (for a celebration); figuratively and commonly, to gloat, to boast triumphantly
definition_in_language: Décorer un lieu de drapeaux pour une fête ; au sens figuré et courant, se réjouir avec ostentation, se vanter d'un succès.
cultural_note: "Il n'y a pas de quoi pavoiser" = "there's nothing to boast about/celebrate here" — a common everyday use of the figurative sense.

translation_en: a puff, a ruche, a gathered fabric flourish (a decorative puffed detail on a garment)
definition_in_language: Ornement de tissu froncé ou gonflé, formant un volume décoratif sur un vêtement — par exemple à la manche ou à la culotte.
source_sentence: Et que le vicomte s'était fait faire un costume de velours noir avec un gros bouillonné à la manche, un autre à la culotte.
cultural_note: Built from the verb "bouillonner" (to bubble/boil; figuratively, to seethe with emotion) — the fashion sense applies the same "bubbling, puffing out" image to gathered fabric rather than liquid or feeling.

translation_en: to curry (a horse or mule — brushing/grooming with a currycomb); figuratively, to give someone a rough time, to thrash/harshly criticize
definition_in_language: Brosser un cheval avec une étrille ; au sens figuré, malmener ou critiquer sévèrement quelqu'un.
source_sentence: Mais lui aussi le vagabond avait fait étriller son pauvre mulet et rapiécer son coude et son genou.
cultural_note: In this sentence it's the literal grooming sense, via the causative "faire + infinitive" construction ("avait fait étriller" = had [someone] curry his mule) — the same pattern as "se faire disputer" and "envoyer chercher."

translation_en: to polish, to shine (through vigorous rubbing — metal, shoes, brass, silverware)
definition_in_language: Frotter vigoureusement un objet, souvent en métal, pour le faire briller.

translation_en: to run one's errands (shopping, small tasks)
definition_in_language: Faire ses achats ou ses petites tâches quotidiennes — synonyme plus ancien ou régional de "faire ses courses."
cultural_note: "Commissions" here means errands/shopping, not the English business sense of "commission" (a fee or a formal task assignment).

translation_en: a wedding procession
definition_in_language: Ensemble des invités et participants qui défilent en procession lors d'un mariage.

translation_en: a bride's trousseau (the collection of clothes, linens, and household items a bride traditionally brought into a marriage)
definition_in_language: Ensemble d'effets personnels et de linge qu'une jeune mariée apportait traditionnellement dans son nouveau foyer.
cultural_note: Same word also commonly means "a bunch of keys" ("un trousseau de clés") — an unrelated everyday sense worth knowing too.

translation_en: crooked, askew, lopsided, off-kilter (in a slightly comic or awkward way)
definition_in_language: De travers, mal aligné, d'une manière légèrement comique ou maladroite.
cultural_note: Near-synonym of "bancal," added earlier. "Guingois" almost never appears outside this fixed phrase.

translation_en: a groomsman, best man (the male equivalent of "demoiselle d'honneur," bridesmaid)
definition_in_language: Jeune homme qui assiste le marié lors d'un mariage, équivalent masculin de la demoiselle d'honneur.

translation_en: an evening gathering (a rural tradition of gathering by the fire in the evening); also, a wake (staying up with the deceased before burial)
definition_in_language: Réunion en soirée, traditionnellement autour du feu, pour discuter ou travailler ensemble ; ou, veillée funèbre, nuit passée auprès d'un défunt avant l'enterrement.
cultural_note: The everyday gathering sense reflects a real French rural tradition — neighbors and family staying up together to talk, tell stories, or do handwork by the fire.

translation_en: mangy, patchy-furred, bald in patches (of an animal's coat)
definition_in_language: Dont le pelage présente des zones sans poils — se dit d'un animal ; littéralement, dépouillé de sa peau ou de son pelage par endroits.
source_sentence: L'un sur son maigre cheval, l'autre sur son mulet pelé.
cultural_note: From "peler," to peel — same underlying image of a surface stripped bare in spots.

translation_en: a fencing master, an arms instructor (a historical formal title/rank)
definition_in_language: Maître d'escrime, instructeur expert dans le maniement des armes — titre historique et formel.
cultural_note: "Prévôt" is an old title for an official/officer holding authority in a specific domain, similar to a provost or guild-master.

translation_en: a dormouse (a small rodent famous for its long winter hibernation)
definition_in_language: Petit rongeur connu pour sa longue hibernation ; a donné l'expression "dormir comme un loir," pour désigner un sommeil profond.
cultural_note: "Dormir comme un loir" = "to sleep like a log" — a common French idiom built directly on this animal's reputation for hibernating heavily.

translation_en: an earthworm (the more technical/precise word — vs. the more casual "ver de terre," same meaning)
definition_in_language: Ver de terre, invertébré vivant dans le sol, utile pour l'agriculture.

translation_en: a fencer (someone who practices/competes in fencing)
definition_in_language: Personne qui pratique l'escrime, sport de combat à l'épée, au fleuret ou au sabre.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "prévôt d'armes," added earlier — the same fencing/combat-sport vocabulary cluster.

translation_en: a parry (a defensive move blocking/deflecting an opponent's attack, in fencing or combat)
definition_in_language: Mouvement défensif visant à bloquer ou dévier l'attaque de l'adversaire, en escrime ou au combat.
cultural_note: "Parade" can also mean a display/procession, as in English — but in a fencing/combat context, it specifically means the defensive block.

translation_en: a feint (a fake attack meant to deceive an opponent into a wrong defensive reaction)
definition_in_language: Mouvement d'attaque simulé, destiné à tromper l'adversaire pour créer une ouverture.
cultural_note: Joins "parade," "escrimeur," and "prévôt d'armes" from the same fencing vocabulary cluster.

translation_en: mastery, expert skill, virtuosity
definition_in_language: Grande habileté, virtuosité dans l'exécution de quelque chose.
cultural_note: Borrowed directly from Italian, keeping the same spelling and general meaning.

translation_en: to riddle with holes, to perforate all over
definition_in_language: Couvrir de nombreux trous, transpercer à plusieurs endroits ; de "cribler," qui signifie littéralement tamiser.
cultural_note: "Cribler" literally means to sift (through a sieve, "un crible"), but is overwhelmingly used figuratively — "criblé de balles" (riddled with bullets), "criblé de dettes" (riddled with debt).

translation_en: hand-to-hand combat, close combat (literally "body to body")
definition_in_language: Combat rapproché, où les adversaires sont au contact direct l'un de l'autre.
source_sentence: À un certain moment, dans un corps à corps les deux gardes se trouvèrent en contact: les pointes de compas étaient fixées dans le sol comme des herses.

translation_en: a harrow (a spiked farming tool dragged over soil); also, a portcullis
definition_in_language: Instrument agricole à dents ou pointes, traîné sur le sol pour ameublir la terre ; ici employé en comparaison pour évoquer des pointes plantées dans le sol.
source_sentence: À un certain moment, dans un corps à corps les deux gardes se trouvèrent en contact: les pointes de compas étaient fixées dans le sol comme des herses.
cultural_note: Used here as a simile — the sharp compass-points stuck in the ground looked "like harrows," a row of spikes.

translation_en: a (mechanical) spring; figuratively, the underlying motive/driving force behind an action; also, "en dernier ressort" = as a last resort
definition_in_language: Pièce mécanique élastique qui se détend (comme dans une horloge ou un matelas) ; au sens figuré, la motivation ou la force qui pousse à agir.

translation_en: a click (sound, or a small releasing mechanism); figuratively, a sudden realization, an "aha" moment
definition_in_language: Bruit sec d'un mécanisme qui se déclenche ; au sens figuré, prise de conscience soudaine, moment où l'on comprend enfin quelque chose.
cultural_note: "Avoir un déclic" is the common way to describe something suddenly clicking into place mentally.

translation_en: to lose one's balance
definition_in_language: Ne plus être stable, être sur le point de tomber.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "bancal" and "de guingois," added earlier.

translation_en: on this side of, short of, below (a threshold or limit) — opposite of "au-delà (de)," beyond
definition_in_language: De ce côté-ci d'une limite (spatiale) ; au sens figuré, en dessous d'un seuil ou d'une attente.

translation_en: beyond (a place, a limit, a threshold) — opposite of "en deçà (de)," on this side of
definition_in_language: De l'autre côté d'une limite (spatiale) ; au sens figuré, ce qui dépasse un seuil ou une attente.
cultural_note: Pairs directly with "en deçà (de)," added just before this — the two are exact opposites, best learned together. Also used as a standalone noun, "l'au-delà," meaning the afterlife/the great beyond.

translation_en: once again, anew, a second time (a fairly archaic/literary adverb)
definition_in_language: De nouveau, encore une fois — terme assez ancien, littéraire, peu usité dans le français parlé moderne.
source_sentence: L'effroi que nous avions ressenti, Trelawney et moi, devint du réconfort à l'idée du danger évité, puis derechef de l'épouvante en raison de l'horrible fin de nos persécuteurs.
cultural_note: Not something you'd hear in everyday modern speech — very much a written-French, older-literature word.

translation_en: an entrechat (a ballet jump where the legs rapidly cross and beat in mid-air)
definition_in_language: Saut de danse classique pendant lequel le danseur croise et décroise rapidement les jambes en l'air.

translation_en: to abandon, to neglect, to forsake (someone or something previously cared for)
definition_in_language: Abandonner, cesser de s'occuper de quelqu'un ou de quelque chose que l'on soignait auparavant.
cultural_note: A fairly formal/literary word, stronger than plain "négliger."

translation_en: chickenpox
definition_in_language: Maladie infantile contagieuse, causée par un virus, provoquant des boutons qui démangent sur tout le corps.

translation_en: erysipelas (a bacterial skin infection producing a raised, sharply-bordered red rash — historically "St. Anthony's Fire")
definition_in_language: Infection bactérienne de la peau, provoquant une plaque rouge, chaude et bien délimitée — appelée historiquement "le feu de saint Antoine."
cultural_note: A genuine, period-accurate illness — fits this book's recurring medical/plague vocabulary (pellagre, miasme, and the leprosy thread).

translation_en: incomplete, full of gaps (knowledge, a text, a record with significant missing pieces)
definition_in_language: Qui présente des lacunes, des manques importants — se dit d'une connaissance, d'un texte ou d'un dossier incomplet.
cultural_note: From "lacune," a gap.

translation_en: a jester, a court fool; more generally, a buffoon, a ridiculous/clownish fool
definition_in_language: Personne dont le rôle était de divertir par des plaisanteries à la cour ; par extension, personne ridicule ou bouffonne.

translation_en: a gulf (the geographic body of water)
definition_in_language: Grande étendue d'eau formant une échancrure dans une côte.

translation_en: to fly [a country's] flag — the standard nautical phrase for a ship's registered nationality/ensign
definition_in_language: Expression maritime signifiant qu'un navire arbore le drapeau d'un pays donné, indiquant sa nationalité d'immatriculation.
cultural_note: "Pavillon" here specifically means a ship's flag/ensign, distinct from the more general "drapeau."

translation_en: a harbor, a roadstead (sheltered coastal water where ships can anchor safely)
definition_in_language: Vaste étendue d'eau abritée près de la côte, où les navires peuvent mouiller en sécurité.
cultural_note: Common idiom: "laisser quelqu'un en rade" = to leave someone stranded/in the lurch.

translation_en: a ship's railing, gunwale (the raised rail along a ship's deck)
definition_in_language: Garde-corps ou rambarde qui borde le pont d'un navire.

translation_en: the masts of a ship, collectively (the whole mast/rigging structure)
definition_in_language: Ensemble des mâts d'un navire.
cultural_note: From "mât," mast.

translation_en: to unfurl banners/streamers
definition_in_language: Déployer des bandes de tissu ou de papier portant un message, souvent lors d'une célébration.

translation_en: pineapple
definition_in_language: Fruit tropical à chair jaune et à peau écailleuse, surmonté d'une touffe de feuilles.

translation_en: a spyglass, a telescope (the handheld, extendable kind, historically used by sailors/explorers)
definition_in_language: Instrument optique portatif, généralement extensible, utilisé pour observer des objets éloignés — synonyme historique de "longue-vue."

translation_en: Tressette (a traditional Italian trick-taking card game, still commonly played today)
definition_in_language: Jeu de cartes italien traditionnel, à plis, souvent joué en équipe de deux paires.
cultural_note: Fits the Italian setting of this book.

translation_en: to hoist aboard, to haul up onto the ship (cargo, a person)
definition_in_language: Soulever et faire monter quelque chose ou quelqu'un sur un navire.

translation_en: to weigh anchor, to set sail (the standard nautical phrase for departing)
definition_in_language: Remonter l'ancre pour permettre au navire de quitter le port ; par extension, partir.

translation_en: a collar (of a coat or shirt)
definition_in_language: Часть одежды, охватывающая шею — например, у пальто или рубашки.
source_sentence: Ничего, ничего, - твердил, умиленно улыбаясь, Николай Петрович и раза два ударил рукою по воротнику сыновней шинели и по собственному пальто.

translation_en: a greatcoat, an overcoat (specifically the long, military-style coat historically worn in Russian/Soviet uniform)
definition_in_language: Длинное форменное пальто, традиционно носимое военными в России.
source_sentence: Ничего, ничего, - твердил, умиленно улыбаясь, Николай Петрович и раза два ударил рукою по воротнику сыновней шинели и по собственному пальто.
cultural_note: Also the title of Gogol's famous short story "Шинель" ("The Overcoat") — one of the most influential works in Russian literature.
image_credit: Russian soldier in a greatcoat (шинель), 1862 — New York Public Library Digital Collections, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (published before 1931).

translation_en: let's have a look at you, come on, show yourself (a warm, informal invitation, not a blunt command)
definition_in_language: Ласковое или неформальное побуждение показать себя, дать на себя посмотреть.
cultural_note: The particle "-ка" tacked onto an imperative softens it into something casual/inviting rather than blunt — "покажи" alone is a flat command ("show!"), while "покажи-ка" reads more like "go on, show me." This particle is a productive pattern that attaches to all kinds of verbs, worth recognizing beyond just this one phrase.

translation_en: a loose, shapeless robe or smock (often with a mildly comic/dismissive connotation — baggy, ill-fitting, old-fashioned)
definition_in_language: Мешковатая, бесформенная одежда, часто с оттенком иронии или насмешки.
source_sentence: Николай Петрович быстро обернулся и, подойдя к человеку высокого роста в длинном балахоне с кистями, только что вышедшему из тарантаса, крепко стиснул его обнажённую красную руку, которую тот не сразу ему подал.

translation_en: a tassel/fringe; also, a paintbrush; also, the hand/wrist — three distinct senses, context-dependent
definition_in_language: 1) Украшение в виде свисающих нитей; 2) инструмент для рисования; 3) часть руки от запястья до кончиков пальцев.
source_sentence: Николай Петрович быстро обернулся и, подойдя к человеку высокого роста в длинном балахоне с кистями, только что вышедшему из тарантаса, крепко стиснул его обнажённую красную руку, которую тот не сразу ему подал.
cultural_note: Genuinely three-way polysemous — here ("с кистями") it's tassels/fringe on the robe, but the same word means paintbrush or the anatomical hand/wrist in other contexts.

translation_en: a historical Russian four-wheeled traveling carriage, springless — suspended on long wooden poles instead of metal springs
definition_in_language: Старинная русская дорожная повозка на четырёх колёсах, без металлических рессор, распространённая в XIX веке.
source_sentence: Николай Петрович быстро обернулся и, подойдя к человеку высокого роста в длинном балахоне с кистями, только что вышедшему из тарантаса, крепко стиснул его обнажённую красную руку, которую тот не сразу ему подал.
cultural_note: In English, this vehicle is usually referred to by its transliterated name, "tarantas" — a real historical type, common for long-distance travel in 19th-century Russia.

translation_en: to grip/squeeze someone's hand tightly (a firm handshake or handclasp)
definition_in_language: Крепко сжать чью-либо руку — например, при рукопожатии.
source_sentence: Николай Петрович быстро обернулся и, подойдя к человеку высокого роста в длинном балахоне с кистями, только что вышедшему из тарантаса, крепко стиснул его обнажённую красную руку, которую тот не сразу ему подал.
cultural_note: From "стиснуть," to clench/squeeze tightly — also used in "стиснуть зубы," to clench one's teeth.

translation_en: flat (physically); figuratively, flat/dull/banal (a lame joke, a trite remark)
definition_in_language: Ровный, без выпуклостей и впадин; в переносном смысле — банальный, скучный, неостроумный (например, о шутке).
cultural_note: "Плоская шутка" = "a flat/lame joke" — a common figurative use.

translation_en: to harness/hitch up the horses (to a carriage, before setting off)
definition_in_language: Запрягать лошадей в повозку перед поездкой.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "тарантас," added earlier — a standard period phrase for preparing to travel.

translation_en: a young master, a gentleman's son (the son of a "барин," a landowning nobleman) — often used with an ironic or critical edge
definition_in_language: Сын барина, молодой дворянин; часто с оттенком иронии, подразумевающим избалованность и незнакомство с трудом.
cultural_note: Ties into the same gentry/serf social divide as "душа" (souls/serfs), added earlier — this novel is deeply concerned with that class tension, set right on the cusp of the 1861 Emancipation.

translation_en: a team of three horses harnessed side by side, pulling a carriage or sleigh
definition_in_language: Упряжка из трёх лошадей, запряжённых рядом, для повозки или саней.
source_sentence: Я здесь с коляской, но и для твоего тарантаса есть тройка, - хлопотливо говорил Николай Петрович.
cultural_note: In English, this is usually called a "troika" — the same word is also used for a grade of "3" (satisfactory) in Russian school grading, or generically for "a set of three" — context tells you which sense applies.

translation_en: fussily, bustlingly, in a busy/flustered manner
definition_in_language: Суетливо, с озабоченной торопливостью — так, как ведёт себя человек, занятый множеством мелких дел или забот.
source_sentence: Я здесь с коляской, но и для твоего тарантаса есть тройка, - хлопотливо говорил Николай Петрович.
cultural_note: From "хлопотливый" (busy, bustling), related to "хлопоты" (fuss, bother, errands).

translation_en: a small ladle/dipper (for scooping/drinking water)
definition_in_language: Уменьшительное от "ковш" — небольшой черпак, используемый, например, для питья воды.
source_sentence: Аркадий пил воду из железного ковшика, принесённого хозяйкой постоялого двора.
cultural_note: Diminutive of "ковш."

translation_en: a coachman, a driver (of a horse-drawn vehicle) — not a horse caretaker
definition_in_language: Кучер, человек, чьей профессией было управлять лошадьми, запряжёнными в повозку — особенно в старой почтовой системе.
source_sentence: Базаров закурил трубку и подошёл к ямщику, отпрягавшему лошадей.
cultural_note: Historically tied to Russia's post-horse relay system — driving travelers and mail between stations. A horse caretaker/groom would instead be "конюх," a different word.

translation_en: to unharness the horses (opposite of "запрягать/закладывать лошадей," to harness)
definition_in_language: Освобождать лошадей от упряжи, распрягать — противоположность "запрягать."
source_sentence: Базаров закурил трубку и подошёл к ямщику, отпрягавшему лошадей.
cultural_note: Direct opposite of "закладывать лошадей," added earlier.

translation_en: a tear, rip, hole (in fabric or clothing) — not "pocket"
definition_in_language: Дыра, разрыв в ткани или одежде.

translation_en: a sheepskin coat (a heavy, fur-lined winter coat, traditionally worn by peasants and coachmen)
definition_in_language: Тяжёлая меховая шуба из овчины, традиционно носимая крестьянами и ямщиками в старой России.
cultural_note: Ties into the same coachman/travel vocabulary cluster as "ямщик," added earlier.
image_credit: Sergey Ivanov, "Peasant in the Sled" (1904-1905), depicting a тулуп — Tatarstan State Museum of Fine Arts, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (artist died 1910).

translation_en: the shaft-horse, the middle horse of a troika (positioned between the shafts, doing the main pulling work)
definition_in_language: Средняя лошадь в тройке, идущая между оглоблями и выполняющая основную тягловую работу, в отличие от боковых "пристяжных" лошадей.
source_sentence: Митюха только шапкой тряхнул и потащил вожжи с потной коренной.
cultural_note: Short for "коренная лошадь" — the noun is dropped once context is established, leaving the adjective to stand in on its own. Ties directly into "тройка," added earlier.

translation_en: a tip, a gratuity (literally "for vodka" — a classic idiom for tipping, not a literal offer of vodka)
definition_in_language: Устойчивое выражение, означающее чаевые, вознаграждение за услугу.
source_sentence: Живей, живей, ребята, подсобляйте, - воскликнул Николай Петрович, - на водку будет!
cultural_note: The old idiomatic way to promise a cash tip — "there'll be [something] for vodka" — not a literal promise to hand out vodka.

translation_en: to help, to lend a hand (a folksy, colloquial/dialectal variant of "помогать")
definition_in_language: Просторечный, диалектный вариант глагола "помогать."
source_sentence: Живей, живей, ребята, подсобляйте, - воскликнул Николай Петрович, - на водку будет!

translation_en: quicker!, look lively!, hurry up! (an exhortation to move faster)
definition_in_language: Восклицание, побуждающее действовать быстрее — "быстрее!", "поживее!"
source_sentence: Живей, живей, ребята, подсобляйте, - воскликнул Николай Петрович, - на водку будет!
cultural_note: Technically the comparative form of "живо" (briskly), used commandingly.

translation_en: to harness/hitch up the horses (perfective aspect -- a completed action)
definition_in_language: Совершенный вид глагола "закладывать" — запрячь лошадей в повозку (законченное действие).
source_sentence: В несколько минут лошади были заложены.
cultural_note: The perfective counterpart of "закладывать лошадей," added earlier — worth practicing as its own entry since Russian verb aspect pairs (imperfective/perfective) are lexically distinct forms, not just a tense conjugation the way English or French would handle it.

translation_en: the coach-box, the driver's seat (the elevated bench at the front of a carriage)
definition_in_language: Сиденье кучера, расположенное впереди повозки.
source_sentence: Пётр взобрался на козлы.
cultural_note: Literally the plural of "козёл" (a billy-goat) — extended metaphorically to name trestle/sawhorse-type support structures generally, and specifically the coachman's seat here.

translation_en: wallpaper (a plural-only noun in Russian, no singular form)
definition_in_language: Материал (обычно бумажный), которым оклеивают стены комнаты.
source_sentence: И комната твоя оклеена обоями.

translation_en: to paper/cover something with something glued on (e.g. wallpaper)
definition_in_language: Покрыть что-либо чем-либо приклеенным (например, обоями).
source_sentence: И комната твоя оклеена обоями.
cultural_note: "Оклеить обоями" is the set phrase for "to wallpaper (a room)." The sentence this was pulled from actually uses the short-form passive participle "оклеена" (agreeing with "комната," feminine) — a productive pattern where the ending shifts by gender/number: оклеен (m), оклеена (f), оклеено (n), оклеены (pl).

translation_en: to be warm/affectionate toward someone, to show kindness and tenderness
definition_in_language: Проявить нежность, доброту, тёплое отношение к кому-либо.
source_sentence: Пожалуйста, папаша, приласкай его.
cultural_note: From "ласка" (affection, tenderness), the same root as "ласкать" (to caress, to be affectionate).

translation_en: a colloquial construction meaning "don't tell me that's...", "surely that's not... is it?" — voicing a suspicion as surprised, tentative doubt rather than a flat statement
definition_in_language: Разговорная конструкция, выражающая удивлённое предположение — говорящий уже подозревает, что это так, но формулирует это как вопрос с оттенком удивления, а не как обычное отрицание.
source_sentence: Это никак наши мужики едут?
cultural_note: A different sense of "никак" than its literal meaning ("no way, not at all" — a plain negation adverb). Here it functions as a colloquial modal particle expressing tentative surprise, not negating anything — the speaker usually already believes the thing they're asking about.

translation_en: unbridled — literally, a horse driven without a bit/bridle; figuratively, unrestrained, wild, dissolute (of behavior)
definition_in_language: Без узды, без удил — о лошади; в переносном смысле — несдержанный, разгульный (о поведении).
source_sentence: Несколько телег, запряжённых разнузданными лошадьми, шибко катились по узкому просёлку.
cultural_note: From "разнуздать," to remove a horse's bridle/bit. Context decides whether the literal (horses) or figurative (unrestrained behavior) sense applies.

translation_en: very, really, quite (a colloquial/dialectal intensifier); or, depending on context, quickly/briskly
definition_in_language: Просторечное наречие: очень, сильно — или, в зависимости от контекста, быстро.
source_sentence: Несколько телег, запряжённых разнузданными лошадьми, шибко катились по узкому просёлку.
cultural_note: Common in folk/peasant speech in 19th-century Russian literature.

translation_en: a country road, a rural dirt road (as opposed to a major paved highway)
definition_in_language: Грунтовая, сельская дорога, в отличие от главного шоссе.
source_sentence: Несколько телег, запряжённых разнузданными лошадьми, шибко катились по узкому просёлку.
cultural_note: Short form of "просёлочная дорога."

translation_en: to utter, to say, to speak (a somewhat literary/archaic verb, more formal than the everyday word for "to say")
definition_in_language: Старинный, литературный глагол, означающий «сказать», «произнести» — часто используется в повествовании художественной литературы.
source_sentence: Точно так-с, - промолвил Пётр.
cultural_note: The "-с" at the end of "так" in this sentence is a separate, genuinely interesting feature — a deferential particle (short for "сударь," sir) historically attached to servant/subordinate speech as a mark of respect toward a social superior. Pyotr is a servant speaking to his employer here.

translation_en: a tavern, a bar — specifically the rough, lower-class kind, not a refined establishment
definition_in_language: Простое, часто неблагородное питейное заведение.
source_sentence: В кабак, - прибавил он презрительно и слегка наклонился к кучеру, как бы ссылаясь на него.

translation_en: a coachman (someone who drives a household's horse-drawn carriage) — distinct from "ямщик," a postal-relay driver
definition_in_language: Слуга, управляющий лошадьми, запряжёнными в экипаж хозяина.
source_sentence: В кабак, - прибавил он презрительно и слегка наклонился к кучеру, как бы ссылаясь на него.
cultural_note: Near-synonym of "ямщик," added earlier — "кучер" is the general word for a personal household coachman, while "ямщик" specifically named a postal/relay-station driver historically.

translation_en: to refer to, to cite, to invoke (someone/something) as support or justification — not an accusation, more like inviting agreement or citing a witness
definition_in_language: Приводить кого-либо или что-либо как довод, подтверждение или источник.
source_sentence: В кабак, - прибавил он презрительно и слегка наклонился к кучеру, как бы ссылаясь на него.

translation_en: literally, temper/tempering (the metallurgical hardening process); figuratively, a person's temperament or mold, shaped by their upbringing or era — as in the set phrase for "a man of the old school"
definition_in_language: Буквально — процесс закаливания металла; в переносном смысле — характер, склад личности, сформированный воспитанием или эпохой.
source_sentence: Но тот даже не пошевельнулся: это был человек старого закала, не разделявший новейших воззрений.

translation_en: trouble, bother, hassle, a fuss to deal with
definition_in_language: Заботы, беспокойство, трудности, связанные с каким-либо делом.
source_sentence: Хлопоты у меня большие с мужиками в нынешнем году, - продолжал Николай Петрович, обращаясь к сыну.
cultural_note: Related to "хлопотливо," added earlier.

translation_en: quitrent — a real historical payment serfs owed their landlord (in money or produce), distinct from "барщина" (labor obligation)
definition_in_language: Денежный или натуральный платёж, который крепостные крестьяне были обязаны платить помещику, в отличие от барщины (трудовой повинности).
source_sentence: Не платят оброка.
cultural_note: Fits the same social/economic thread as "душа" and "барич," added earlier. The novel is set in 1859 — before the actual 1861 Emancipation Manifesto, though published in 1862, just after it. So this scene reflects the pre-Emancipation years already destabilizing: rumors and public debate about impending reform were circulating widely before the law passed, and peasants were increasingly emboldened to resist old obligations like oброк even before serfdom was formally abolished.

translation_en: to say something through gritted teeth — muttering tersely, reluctantly, with restrained irritation or anger
definition_in_language: Сказать что-либо неохотно, раздражённо, сквозь стиснутые зубы — часто с оттенком сдерживаемого гнева.
cultural_note: Literally "to strain/filter through the teeth," from "процедить" (to strain a liquid, e.g. through a sieve).

translation_en: to incite, to egg someone on, to instigate (goading someone into an action, especially resistance/disobedience)
definition_in_language: Подстрекать, побуждать кого-либо к какому-либо действию — здесь, скорее всего, к неповиновению или сопротивлению.
source_sentence: Подбивают их, вот что беда. Ну, и настоящего страдания все еще нету.
cultural_note: Also has literal senses (to line/quilt something, to reinforce from underneath) and a colloquial sense (to injure, or to shoot down a plane) — context here confirms the figurative "incite" sense.

translation_en: a harness (the collective tack/gear used to harness a horse — straps, bridle, etc.)
definition_in_language: Совокупность ремней и снаряжения, используемых для запряжки лошади.
source_sentence: Сбрую портят.
cultural_note: Fits the equestrian vocab cluster from this book — тройка, коренная, ямщик, кучер.

translation_en: to spoil, to damage, to ruin, to destroy
definition_in_language: Приводить в негодность, повреждать, уничтожать что-либо.
source_sentence: Сбрую портят.

translation_en: to plow (the land)
definition_in_language: Обрабатывать землю плугом перед посевом.
source_sentence: Пахали, впрочем, ничего.
cultural_note: In this sentence, "ничего" is used in its very common colloquial sense of "not bad, okay, alright" — not its literal meaning "nothing."

translation_en: a well-known proverb: "it'll all work out in the end," "this too shall pass" (literally, "it will all get ground up, there will be flour")
definition_in_language: Известная пословица, означающая, что трудности и неприятности со временем разрешатся сами собой.
source_sentence: Перемелется - мука будет.
cultural_note: A classic saying of resigned optimism, similar in spirit to the English idiom "this too shall pass."

translation_en: an awning (canvas, over a balcony or window, for shade) — a homograph of an unrelated noble title for a woman
definition_in_language: Полотняный навес над окном или балконом, защищающий от солнца.
source_sentence: Я с северной стороны над балконом большую маркизу приделал, - промолвил Николай Петрович.
cultural_note: Same spelling, unrelated meaning: this word is also the noble title "marquise." A perfectly-timed callback in the scene, too — Nikolai Petrovich directly answering Arkady's earlier remark about the estate having no shade.

translation_en: to grumble, to grouse, to be peevish (habitually muttering complaints in a grumpy, dissatisfied manner)
definition_in_language: Постоянно и раздражённо жаловаться, ворчать по мелочам.

translation_en: a steward, bailiff, estate manager (someone who ran a landowner's estate on their behalf); in a shop context, a clerk/salesman
definition_in_language: Управляющий имением, ведущий хозяйственные дела помещика от его имени.

translation_en: a manumitted/freed serf — someone granted personal freedom by their owner, distinct from the general 1861 Emancipation
definition_in_language: Крепостной крестьянин, получивший личную свободу от своего владельца — в отличие от всеобщего освобождения крестьян в 1861 году.
cultural_note: Used in this novel to describe Bazarov's own humbler, non-noble family background — a real class contrast with the aristocratic Kirsanovs. Individual landowners could and did free specific serfs well before the general 1861 Emancipation, as a personal act.

translation_en: a household serf — someone who worked in/around the manor house as a domestic servant, distinct from field-working peasants
definition_in_language: Крепостной, служивший в барском доме или на усадьбе (слуга, повар, кучер и т.п.), в отличие от крестьянина, обрабатывающего землю.
cultural_note: From "двор" (courtyard, the manor grounds/household). Fits the same serfdom-era class vocabulary as "оброк," "вольноотпущенный," "барич," and "душа" from this book.

translation_en: a valet, a personal manservant (handling clothing, grooming, and personal errands for a gentleman)
definition_in_language: Личный слуга господина, занимающийся его одеждой, туалетом и личными поручениями — заимствование из немецкого языка.
cultural_note: Borrowed from German "Kammerdiener," literally "chamber servant" — not a native Russian word.

translation_en: a member of the urban lower-middle class in Imperial Russia (small shopkeepers, artisans, low-level clerks) — an official social estate
definition_in_language: Городской житель низшего сословия — мелкий торговец, ремесленник или служащий; официальное сословие в Российской империи.
cultural_note: "Мещанский/мещанство" later took on a strong pejorative meaning — "petty bourgeois," "philistine," narrow-minded and materialistic — a connotation already present in 19th-century usage, not just a later Soviet-era coinage.

translation_en: to preface, to give advance notice/warning of something beforehand (a fairly formal/literary verb)
definition_in_language: Заранее сообщить, предупредить о чём-либо; или предшествовать чему-либо.
cultural_note: Related to "предварительный" (preliminary).

translation_en: to change, to alter, to switch (something)
definition_in_language: Сделать иным, заменить одно другим.
cultural_note: Related to "перемена" (a change).

translation_en: a wing, annex, or small outbuilding/cottage on an estate's grounds
definition_in_language: Небольшая пристройка или отдельное строение на территории усадьбы.
source_sentence: Флигелек-то плох - вот беда.
cultural_note: "Флигелек" is the diminutive form of this word — "the little wing/cottage." Same "вот беда" pattern ("that's the trouble") as earlier estate-disrepair complaints in this book.

translation_en: I feel ashamed, I feel guilty (an impersonal construction, same pattern as other predicate adverbs like "жаль" or "стыдно")
definition_in_language: Испытывать чувство стыда, вины — безличная конструкция, от слова «совесть».
cultural_note: From "совесть" (conscience). The pronoun swaps for who feels it — "мне совестно" (I feel ashamed), "ему совестно" (he feels ashamed), etc.

translation_en: do me a favor (an informal imperative request — can be sincere or sarcastic/irritated depending on tone)
definition_in_language: Вежливая (или, в зависимости от тона, раздражённая) просьба о любезности.
cultural_note: "Одолжение" = a favor, a kindness. Same double-edged tone range as English "do me a favor."

translation_en: to clear-cut, to fell an entire forest (a specific fixed collocation with its own distinct meaning)
definition_in_language: Полностью вырубить лес, уничтожить лесной массив.
cultural_note: "Сводить" alone has several unrelated common meanings depending on context — to take someone somewhere and bring them back, to reconcile/bring together, "сводить с ума" (to drive someone crazy). This specific "clear a forest" sense is a distinct fixed collocation.

translation_en: moreover, besides, what's more (a connective phrase adding an additional point or reason)
definition_in_language: Кроме того, вдобавок — вводное слово, добавляющее ещё один довод или обстоятельство.
cultural_note: Similar in function to "к тому же."

translation_en: picturesque, scenic (literally "picture-like")
definition_in_language: Красивый, достойный быть изображённым на картине — о пейзаже, местности.
source_sentence: Места, по которым они проезжали, не могли назваться живописными.
cultural_note: From "живопись" (painting, art).

translation_en: the sky, the firmament, the vault of heaven (a more poetic/literary word for sky)
definition_in_language: Видимое небесное пространство, особенно у горизонта — более поэтичное слово, чем простое «небо».
cultural_note: From "небо" (sky) + "склон" (slope) — evoking the visual curve where sky meets horizon.

translation_en: to rise, to swell, to heave (upward) — a heaving chest, rising waves, billowing dust or smoke (a fairly literary verb)
definition_in_language: Подниматься, вздуваться — например, о груди при тяжёлом дыхании, о волнах, о пыли.

translation_en: to wind, to meander, to coil, to snake (a path, river, or ravine twisting through terrain)
definition_in_language: Изгибаться, тянуться извилистой линией — о дороге, реке, овраге.
source_sentence: Вились овраги.

translation_en: a ravine, a gully
definition_in_language: Глубокая впадина в почве, образованная эрозией, обычно вытянутая и извилистая.
source_sentence: Вились овраги.

translation_en: Catherine's era — the reign of Catherine the Great (Catherine II, ruled 1762–1796)
definition_in_language: Период правления Екатерины II (1762–1796).
source_sentence: Вились овраги, напоминая глазу их собственное изображение на старинных планах екатерининского времени.
cultural_note: Shown here in the sentence in genitive case ("екатерининского времени," modifying "планах") — stored in the nominative as the more flexible base form to actually learn. Catherine the Great's reign included a famous large-scale land-surveying/cadastral mapping project (the General Land Survey), which produced exactly the kind of old topographic "plans" referenced in this sentence — a genuinely specific historical detail, not just a vague nod to "old times."

translation_en: dug around, surrounded by a trench/ditch (e.g. a moat around a building)
definition_in_language: Окружённый вырытой канавой или рвом.
cultural_note: Past passive participle of "обрыть" (to dig a trench around something).

translation_en: a dam
definition_in_language: Сооружение, перегораживающее реку или пруд для удержания воды.
source_sentence: Крошечные пруды с худыми плотинами.

translation_en: a traditional Russian peasant log house/cabin
definition_in_language: Традиционный русский крестьянский дом, обычно бревенчатый.
source_sentence: Избёнками.
cultural_note: "Избёнка" is its diminutive-pejorative form — a small, shabby, run-down hut, not just an affectionate "little house." Fits this passage's whole picture of rural decline (leaky dams, tiny ponds).

translation_en: a village
definition_in_language: Населённый пункт сельского типа.
source_sentence: Деревеньки.
cultural_note: "Деревенька" is its diminutive form — the suffix "-еньк-" tends to be softer/more neutral or affectionate, unlike the belittling "-ёнк-" in words like "избёнка."

translation_en: scattered, blown apart, strewn about (often by wind or force — e.g. a roof half blown apart, hay scattered around)
definition_in_language: Разбросанный, раскиданный в разные стороны — часто под воздействием ветра или силы.
cultural_note: Past passive participle of "размести/разметать" (to scatter, to sweep apart).

translation_en: to thresh (grain — separating it from husks/stalks)
definition_in_language: Отделять зёрна от колосьев, обычно ударами или с помощью машины.
source_sentence: Молотильные сарайчики.

translation_en: a shed, a barn
definition_in_language: Хозяйственная постройка для хранения инструментов, сена или скота.
source_sentence: Молотильные сарайчики.
cultural_note: "Сарайчики" (diminutive plural) = "little sheds" — the form that appeared in the text.

translation_en: brushwood, kindling — dry twigs and small branches
definition_in_language: Сухие ветки и сучья, собираемые для растопки или для плетения изгороди.
cultural_note: Also the name of a traditional Russian fried pastry — thin, crispy fried dough twists — named for their resemblance to little bundles of kindling.

translation_en: a threshing floor/barnyard (the designated area or structure where harvested grain was threshed and stored)
definition_in_language: Место или сооружение для молотьбы и хранения зерна.
cultural_note: Fits alongside "молотить" and "сарай," added earlier.

translation_en: plaster, stucco (a construction material used to coat walls/ceilings)
definition_in_language: Строительный материал, наносимый на стены или потолки для выравнивания поверхности и отделки.

translation_en: ruined, devastated, laid waste, bankrupted
definition_in_language: Приведённый в упадок, разрушенный, лишённый средств — причастие от «разорить».

translation_en: shabby, worn out, threadbare, tattered (a colloquial adjective)
definition_in_language: Поношенный, потрёпанный, обветшавший от долгого использования — разговорное слово.

translation_en: a nag — a broken-down, worn-out old horse (often used with contempt)
definition_in_language: Старая, изнурённая, никудышная лошадь — часто с пренебрежительным оттенком.
source_sentence: Клячонках.
cultural_note: "Клячонка" is its diminutive-pejorative form, which is the form that appeared in the text. Ties back to the equestrian vocabulary cluster from earlier in this book, but in a distinctly unflattering register.

translation_en: a willow tree (specifically a broadleaf/purple willow — a close relative of "ива," the general word for willow)
definition_in_language: Вид ивы с гибкими ветвями, растущей обычно у воды.
cultural_note: A recurring image in Russian folk poetry and songs.

translation_en: to graze, to nibble (grass) — of animals
definition_in_language: О животных — щипать траву, пастись, отрывая небольшие пучки зубами.
cultural_note: This same verb also means "to pinch," "to pluck" (feathers, petals), and "to sting/bite" (of cold) — context decides which sense applies.

translation_en: a claw, a talon (of an animal or bird)
definition_in_language: Твёрдый острый отросток на пальце животного или птицы.

translation_en: joyless, cheerless, bleak, comfortless
definition_in_language: Не дающий утешения или радости; унылый, мрачный.
cultural_note: From "без" (without) + "отрада" (joy, comfort, solace).

translation_en: a lark (the bird, famous for its song, associated with pastoral/dawn imagery)
definition_in_language: Небольшая певчая птица, известная своим звонким пением, часто взлетающая высоко в небо.

translation_en: to burst into song, to pour forth in trilling song (a standard literary way to describe continuous, warbling birdsong)
definition_in_language: Заливаться пением/трелью — непрерывно, звонко петь, особенно о птицах.
source_sentence: Звонкими струйками заливались жаворонки.
cultural_note: The image here compares the larks' continuous trilling song to little clear, ringing rivulets of sound ("звонкими струйками").

translation_en: a rook (a black corvid bird — a specific crow-family species)
definition_in_language: Чёрная птица из семейства врановых.
cultural_note: "Грачи прилетели" ("The Rooks Have Returned") is the title of one of the most famous, beloved Russian paintings (by Savrasov), and rooks arriving is the classic folk marker of spring's arrival in Russia, much like robins in English-speaking culture.

translation_en: rye (the grain crop)
definition_in_language: Злаковое растение, из зерна которого делают ржаной хлеб и муку.
source_sentence: Во ржи.
cultural_note: Irregular declension — genitive/prepositional is "ржи." "Во ржи" uses "во" instead of "в" before this consonant cluster, for euphonic reasons.

translation_en: to pour out, to stream out, to come pouring out all at once (of a crowd/group)
definition_in_language: О группе людей — выйти куда-либо сразу, толпой.
source_sentence: Толпа дворовых не высыпала на крыльцо встречать господ.
cultural_note: This scene implies a customary welcome ritual (a crowd of servants greeting the returning masters) notably failing to happen — fitting the thread of estate disorder/decline running through recent chapters.

translation_en: livery (adjective) — relating to a servant's uniform livery
definition_in_language: Относящийся к ливрее — форменной одежде слуг.
cultural_note: From "ливрея" (livery, the uniform itself). "Ливрейный лакей" = a liveried footman.

translation_en: a crested button — a button bearing a coat of arms/crest (common on formal servant livery)
definition_in_language: Пуговица с изображением герба — эмблемы рода, города или государства.
cultural_note: From "герб" (coat of arms, crest). "Гербовый" also has a separate bureaucratic sense — "гербовая бумага" = official stamped paper for legal documents.

translation_en: to unfasten, to unbuckle, to unclip (a strap, button, or buckle)
definition_in_language: Расстегнуть, освободить что-либо застёгнутое или пристёгнутое.
source_sentence: Он молча отворил дверцу коляски и отстегнул фартук тарантаса.

translation_en: an apron — most commonly the everyday clothing item, but here (of a carriage) a protective apron-like flap/covering over the seat, shielding occupants from mud and splashes
definition_in_language: Обычно — предмет одежды для защиты от загрязнения; здесь — защитный полог или покрытие в экипаже, по форме напоминающее фартук.
source_sentence: Он молча отворил дверцу коляски и отстегнул фартук тарантаса.
cultural_note: Tagged archaic specifically for this carriage-cover sense — the everyday "apron (clothing)" sense of the word is still completely current and common.

translation_en: a peaked cap (a soft cap with a visor, traditionally worn by merchants, peasants, or working men in 19th-century Russia)
definition_in_language: Мягкий головной убор с козырьком, традиционно носимый мужчинами низших сословий в XIX веке.
image_credit: Vasily Vereshchagin, "A Boy in a Black Kartuz" (1880-1901), depicting a картуз — Kyiv National Art Gallery, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (published before 1931).

translation_en: bad, poor, in bad condition, worn out — an older/dialectal sense, distinct from the far more common modern meaning "thin"
definition_in_language: Плохой, испорченный, ветхий — устаревшее или диалектное значение, отличное от современного «худой» = тощий.
cultural_note: Genuinely easy to default to the wrong meaning ("thin") since that sense is so much more common today. Also the root of the idiom "не худо" ("wouldn't be a bad idea").

translation_en: wouldn't be a bad idea, wouldn't hurt to... (a litotes/understatement construction — literally "not bad," used to mean something is actually quite desirable)
definition_in_language: Литота: буквально «не плохо», используется, чтобы сказать, что что-либо было бы весьма желательно.
source_sentence: Поесть действительно не худо.
cultural_note: Built on "худой" in its older "bad" sense, added alongside this entry.

translation_en: a tailcoat, a formal dress coat (men's formal evening wear with tails)
definition_in_language: Мужской парадный костюм с длинными фалдами сзади, для торжественных случаев.

translation_en: a kerchief, a headscarf, or a handkerchief (depending on context/size)
definition_in_language: Кусок ткани, обычно квадратной формы — носовой платок или головной платок (косынка).
cultural_note: "Платочек" is its diminutive form — the form that appeared in the text.

translation_en: to grin, to smirk, to bare one's teeth in a smile (a literary/dated verb, often with an unpleasant, forced, or servile connotation)
definition_in_language: Улыбнуться, оскалив зубы — часто с оттенком неестественности, натянутости или подобострастия.

translation_en: lacquered, patent-leather (shiny, glossy leather)
definition_in_language: Блестящий, покрытый лаком — о коже, обуви.

translation_en: half-boots, ankle boots
definition_in_language: Обувь, закрывающая ногу до середины голени.
source_sentence: Лаковые полусапожки.
cultural_note: From "полу-" (half) + "сапоги" (boots). "Полусапожки" is its diminutive plural — the form that appeared in the text.

translation_en: literally, bilious; figuratively, sour, embittered, cynical, irritable (of a person's temperament or expression)
definition_in_language: Буквально — относящийся к желчи; в переносном смысле — раздражённый, озлобленный, циничный.
source_sentence: Желчное лицо.
cultural_note: From "желчь" (bile).

translation_en: a chisel, a graver/burin (a sculptor's or engraver's cutting tool)
definition_in_language: Инструмент скульптора или гравёра для вырезания, высекания.
source_sentence: Лицо его, желчное, но без морщин, необыкновенно правильное и чистое, словно выведенное тонким и лёгким резцом.
cultural_note: Also has a separate anatomical sense — an incisor (front cutting tooth) — context decides which applies. Here it's the sculptural simile: a face as if carved with a fine, light chisel.

translation_en: oblong, elongated (a shape longer than it is wide — often used for a face shape)
definition_in_language: Имеющий удлинённую форму — длиннее, чем шире.

translation_en: a precious gemstone known for its shifting, iridescent play of color
definition_in_language: Драгоценный камень, известный своей радужной игрой света.
source_sentence: Рукавчика, застёгнутого одиноким крупным опалом.
cultural_note: Known in English by the same name, "opal."

translation_en: nephew
definition_in_language: Сын брата или сестры по отношению к дяде или тёте.

translation_en: a figure, a build, a waist (a person's physique) — a word with unrelated senses too: a camp/encampment, or a mill/works
definition_in_language: Телосложение человека, особенно талия — «стройный стан» = стройная фигура.
source_sentence: Пётр Петрович слегка наклонил свой гибкий стан.
cultural_note: Context decides the sense — here it's the physique/build meaning, describing a small, elegant bow.

translation_en: to dawdle, to linger, to hesitate briefly, to be slow to act
definition_in_language: Задержаться, промедлить, проявить нерешительность на короткое время.

translation_en: literally, to loosen up/shake off stiffness (physically); figuratively, to become sharper, more worldly, to lose one's naivety (often after a new experience — travel, university, city life)
definition_in_language: Littéralement, perdre sa raideur physique en bougeant ; au sens figuré, devenir plus vif, plus dégourdi, moins naïf — souvent après une expérience nouvelle.
source_title: Отцы и дети (Fathers and Sons) — a French phrase embedded in the Russian text, a period-accurate detail since 19th-century Russian aristocrats spoke French socially
cultural_note: Spotted in a Russian novel, not a French one — Turgenev sprinkles genuine French into the text since French was the primary social language of the Russian aristocracy at the time.

translation_en: to wind a clock/watch
definition_in_language: Заводить механизм часов, поворачивая заводной ключ или головку.
cultural_note: The "start/wind up a mechanism" sense of "заводить."

translation_en: to make friends
definition_in_language: Приобретать друзей, знакомиться и сближаться с новыми людьми.
cultural_note: The "acquire, start having something new" sense — same sense as "заводить машины" from this book.

translation_en: to strike up a conversation
definition_in_language: Начать беседу с кем-либо.
cultural_note: The "start/initiate" sense (a conversation, a song).

translation_en: to start a car (the engine)
definition_in_language: Запустить двигатель автомобиля.
cultural_note: A nice callback/contrast to "заводить машины" from this book (1859-set, meaning "acquire farm machinery") — same words, but modern "машина" defaults to "car," and this phrase uses the mechanism-starting sense of "заводить" rather than the acquiring sense.

translation_en: to lead someone somewhere (physically) — sometimes with a connotation of leading astray
definition_in_language: Привести кого-либо куда-либо, ведя его за собой.
cultural_note: The "lead somewhere" sense — e.g. "завести в лес" (to lead into the woods).

translation_en: to suck on/draw repeatedly at a (smoking) pipe
definition_in_language: Затягиваться, посасывая курительную трубку.
cultural_note: From "сосать" (to suck). "Трубка" = a (smoking) pipe.

translation_en: dandyism as a style choice -- fashionable flair, pride in one's appearance (can be neutral or admiring, not necessarily mocking)
definition_in_language: Чрезмерная забота о щёгольском, модном внешнем виде; щегольские манеры.
cultural_note: From "щёголь" (a dandy, a fop) -- centers on style/appearance itself. Compare фатство (id 589), which centers on vanity/conceit as a character flaw rather than the clothes themselves.

translation_en: to turn someone's head, to charm, to infatuate, to make someone swoon
definition_in_language: Очаровывать, вызывать сильное увлечение или влюблённость — буквально, заставлять голову кружиться.
source_sentence: Кружить голову женщинам.

translation_en: to be a "lion" — a dashing, fashionable, socially dominant man; a ladies' man, a society heartthrob (a figurative idiom, not the literal animal)
definition_in_language: В переносном смысле — быть модным, обаятельным светским мужчиной, пользующимся большим успехом у женщин.
source_sentence: Ведь он львом был в своё время.
cultural_note: Ties directly to "кружить голову" and "щегольство," added just before this — this character was a real charmer/dandy in his prime.

translation_en: to captivate, to enchant, to charm, to enthrall someone
definition_in_language: Очаровывать, покорять чьё-либо сердце — буквально, брать в плен.
source_sentence: Пленять-то здесь, жаль, некого.
cultural_note: Related to "плен" (captivity) — literally "to take captive," figuratively "to capture someone's heart."

translation_en: out of old habit, from force of habit, for old times' sake
definition_in_language: По привычке, оставшейся с прежних времён.
source_sentence: По старой, значит, памяти.

translation_en: squire (a knight's attendant); also, an equestrian/horseman
definition_in_language: Jeune noble au service d'un chevalier, qu'il accompagnait et assistait, notamment à la guerre.
source_sentence: Il était suivi d'un écuyer appelé Kurt.
cultural_note: A squire (écuyer) was a young nobleman training to become a knight, serving and accompanying one in combat and daily life. The word comes from 'écu' (shield), since a squire originally carried his lord's shield. Today 'écuyer' also refers to an accomplished horseman or riding master — most famously the écuyers of the Cadre Noir in Saumur, France's elite classical riding academy.

translation_en: stork (bird)
definition_in_language: Grand oiseau migrateur au long bec et aux longues pattes, connu pour nicher sur les toits et les cheminées.
source_sentence: De blancs vols de cigognes traversaient, près de terre, l'air opaque et figé.
cultural_note: Storks carry real folklore weight across Europe — the "storks bring babies" legend is pan-European, and in Alsace (France) the stork is a beloved regional symbol, with a real conservation effort after the population nearly disappeared there in the mid-20th century. They're also strongly associated with Central and Eastern Europe generally, fitting for a book with scenes set in Bohemia.

translation_en: frozen, still, motionless, fixed
definition_in_language: Qui est devenu immobile, sans mouvement ; qui s'est comme solidifié.
source_sentence: De blancs vols de cigognes traversaient, près de terre, l'air opaque et figé.

translation_en: wading bird (a long-legged bird adapted to shallow water — storks, herons, cranes, flamingos, etc.)
definition_in_language: Oiseau caractérisé par de longues pattes, adapté à la vie dans les zones humides et marécageuses.
source_sentence: Qu'est-ce qui peut bien attirer ces échassiers sur les champs de bataille, Kurt?

translation_en: to dry up, to run dry (of a water source — a river, a spring, a well)
definition_in_language: S'assécher complètement, ne plus avoir d'eau ; se dit d'un cours d'eau ou d'une source.
source_sentence: Eux aussi se nourrissent de chair humaine, répondit l'écuyer, maintenant que la famine a rendu la campagne aride et que la sécheresse a tari les fleuves.

translation_en: flamingo (formal/literary register — the everyday word is 'flamant' or 'flamant rose')
definition_in_language: Grand échassier au plumage rose ; terme littéraire ou scientifique pour "flamant".
source_sentence: Là où il y a des cadavres, les cigognes, les phénicoptères et les grues remplacent les vautours et les corbeaux.
cultural_note: The word comes from Greek — 'phoinix' (crimson/purple-red) + 'pteron' (wing), literally "purple-winged." It's also the actual scientific genus name (Phoenicopterus). Dumas-and-Calvino-era literary French reaches for this kind of Greek-rooted term where everyday French would just say 'flamant.'

translation_en: crane (bird)
definition_in_language: Grand oiseau échassier migrateur, au long cou et aux longues pattes.
source_sentence: Là où il y a des cadavres, les cigognes, les phénicoptères et les grues remplacent les vautours et les corbeaux.
cultural_note: Worth knowing the idiom "faire le pied de grue" — literally "to do the crane's foot" — meaning to wait around for a long time, standing about. Comes from a crane's habit of standing motionless on one leg for long stretches.
image_credit: Photo by Andreas Trepte, www.avi-fauna.info, Common Crane (Grus grus), via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 2.5.

translation_en: crow, raven
definition_in_language: Grand oiseau noir, souvent associé à la mort ou aux mauvais présages.
source_sentence: Là où il y a des cadavres, les cigognes, les phénicoptères et les grues remplacent les vautours et les corbeaux.
cultural_note: In French, 'corbeau' also refers to someone who sends anonymous poison-pen letters — a meaning popularized by the 1943 French film Le Corbeau. More broadly, crows and ravens carry strong death/carrion symbolism across many cultures, directly relevant to this battlefield scene.
image_credit: Photo by Frank Schulenburg, Common Raven (Corvus corax), Point Reyes National Seashore, via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0.

translation_en: vibrant, thrilling, exciting, hectic, pulsating with energy — NOT 'trembling with fear' despite resembling English 'trepidation'
definition_in_language: Qui est plein d'agitation et d'énergie intense ; palpitant, exaltant.
